notes: Original 1975 code; updated version. NEA is the largest teacher union in the US with ~3 million members. Two principles: Commitment to the Student, Commitment to the Profession.
Adopted October 2018 by AFT Executive Council; revised July 2023. AFT has ~1.7 million members. Separate from the MCEE which AFT co-developed with NEA.
Founded 1994. Four principles: Students and Learning, Professional Practice, Colleagues, Community and Parents. Independent non-union alternative to NEA/AFT.

organization: National Association of State Directors of Teacher Education and Certification
document_title: Model Code of Ethics for Educators (MCEE), 2nd Edition
notes: First edition 2015; 2nd edition June 2023. Multi-stakeholder consensus code developed with NEA, AFT, NASSP, NAESP, CCSSO, and AACTE. Five principles, 18 sections, 86 standards. Widely adopted by states as basis for teacher licensure ethics requirements.
Formed 2017 by merger of NUT (National Union of Teachers, 1870) and ATL (Association of Teachers and Lecturers). Code embedded in union rules Appendix A. ~450,000 members.

document_title: International Code of Ethics for Educators
notes: Released October 5, 2018. Education International is the global federation representing ~400 education unions in 170 countries (~32 million members). Covers professional values, student relationships, societal responsibility, and digital ethics.

organization: National Association for the Education of Young Children
document_title: Code of Ethics for Early Childhood Educators
notes: First adopted 1989; revised 2005, 2011; draft revision 2024. Covers birth through age 8. Addresses responsibilities to children, families, colleagues, employers, communities, and society. Accompanied by Statement of Commitment. Widely used in ECE preparation programs.

document_title: CEC Ethical Principles and Practice Standards
notes: CEC is the primary professional organization for special education worldwide. Ethical principles include: maintaining challenging expectations, promoting participation, using evidence-based practice, protecting safety, and practicing within professional ethics. Covers initial and advanced preparation standards.

organization: National Association of Elementary School Principals
document_title: Statement of Ethics for School Administrators
notes: Shared statement with NASSP (both co-authored as school administrator ethics). Recently updated 2023. Emphasizes student well-being as primary priority, transcending political and personal biases.

organization: National Association of Secondary School Principals
notes: Reflects Mission Statement, Strategic Objectives, Statement of Ethics for School Administrators, and Policy Statements. Together with NAESP, NASSP co-authored the Professional Standards for Educational Leaders (PSEL 2015) through the National Policy Board for Educational Administration.

Originally adopted 1966; revised 1987 and 2009. Addresses responsibilities to subject/scholarship, students, colleagues, institution, and community. Foundational document for academic professional ethics in the US.

document_title: ASCA Ethical Standards for School Counselors
notes: Updated 2022 in consultation with state associations, counselor educators, and practitioners nationwide. Addresses responsibilities to students, parents, school, community, and self. Covers confidentiality, technology use, cultural competence, and dual relationships.

Effective July 1, 2020. Part of NASP 2020 Professional Standards (four components: practice, graduate preparation, credentialing, ethics). Members and NCSP certification holders are bound to comply. Four sections: Dignity and Rights, Professional Competence and Responsibility, Honesty and Integrity, Responsibility to Schools/Families/Society.

document_title: Code of Ethics of the American Library Association
notes: Most recent amendment 2021 added ninth principle on racial and social justice. Nine core principles covering intellectual freedom, privacy, confidentiality, service equity, honesty in information provision, and professional development. Used by librarians, library staff, and information professionals.

organization: Chartered Institute of Library and Information Professionals
document_title: CILIP Ethical Principles and Code of Professional Practice
notes: All members sign up to CILIP's ethical principles and code on joining. Royal Chartered body for library and information professionals. Ethics Committee provides guidance and periodic reviews. Covers human rights, equality and diversity, professional conduct, stewardship, confidentiality, and professional development.

organization: International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions
document_title: IFLA Code of Ethics for Librarians and other Information Workers
notes: Endorsed by IFLA Governing Board August 2012. Draws on national codes from 60+ countries. Short and full versions available. Covers access to information, privacy, transparency, professional conduct, equality, and knowledge economy. Over 1,400 member organizations in 140 countries.

document_title: SAA Core Values Statement and Code of Ethics for Archivists
notes: Significant revision approved August 2020. Original code introduced in 1980. Jointly used with Core Values of Archivists. Covers collection policies, preservation, access, privacy, donor relations, and professional relationships.

ARMA International is the professional association for records and information management (RIM). Code addresses three areas: society, employers, and the profession. Key principles include supporting free flow of information, maintaining accuracy, confidentiality, avoiding conflicts of interest.
